Game reduces to: LB picks ≤ n+1 pieces (composition of 1), XY subdivides with ≤ n cuts, payoff = alternating sum $D = p_1 - p_2 + p_3 - \\cdots$; LB share $= (1+D)/2$.","note":"Correct reduction is stated, but optimal greedy play is only asserted, not argued."},"L3.2":{"established":"no","quote":"Part B (XY always forces $D\\le T_n$) still open: best candidate \"min over subsets of greedy chain $\\le T_n S$\" — needs verification & proof.","note":"The pigeonhole attempt has a recognized realizability gap; no universal Xiang construction is proved."},"L3.3":{"established":"yes","quote":"family $a_1\\le\\cdots\\le a_m$ super-increasing with margin $\\delta$ ($a_1\\ge\\delta$, $a_{i+1}\\ge\\delta+a_1+\\cdots+a_i$), subdivided with $\\le m-1$ cuts ⇒ $D\\ge\\delta$. Proof: take optimal matching $\\mu$; build multigraph on pieces (edge = matched pair of fragments, unmatched frag = mark).","note":"The matching, tree-component, slack, signed-sum, and block-lemma argument covers arbitrary replies and all n."}},"S_ref":1,"notes":"The lower bound is substantively argued for the geometric division. The upper bound remains explicitly open, and the claiming-phase reduction lacks its promised proof."}
